## 固定收益市場主論

美國公債早盤受強勁消費支出壓抑，隨後新一波科技系統故障促使投資人轉向公債避險，帶動價格由跌轉漲。10年期殖利率下降2.43個基點至5.1068%，2年期下降2.53個基點至4.8041%。本次回升由實質殖利率下滑帶動，通膨補償則小幅上升，與前一交易日油價下跌帶來的紓解不同。

美國國家安全局（NSA）一個通訊網路傳出故障後，市場對科技公司及AI投資熱潮的不安加深，避險買盤隨之增強。標普500下跌1.03%，那斯達克100下跌0.72%。同時，聯準會官員的討論愈來愈聚焦於升息速度：Alberto Musalem主張春季前應多次升息，John Williams則認為無須大幅行動，並將AI帶動的成長能否持續，列為進一步緊縮的部分判斷依據。

不同借款人的融資待遇持續分化。Pimco認為資料中心建設放緩，可改善由大型雲端業者承租的資料中心債券相對定價；另一方面，一筆銀行貸款折價出售，也凸顯個別開發案的疑慮。銀行下調CCC Intelligent Solutions收購融資的借款成本，摩根大通則預測槓桿貸款違約率將明顯上升。當日美債避險需求再度增加，部分借款人仍能取得資金，進口成本上升與住宅市場壓力也日益顯現。

## 美債盤中翻揚，消費與進口成本仍強

10月零售銷售公布後，美債殖利率一度上升。當日AMP經濟日曆顯示，最重要的需求訊號是控制組銷售月增0.6%，高於預測的0.4%及前值0.5%。整體零售銷售月增0.2%，符合預期，但低於前值0.8%。從結構來看，消費的基礎動能比整體增幅放緩所呈現的更強。

接近中午時行情出現轉折。據Bloomberg報導，CNN報導NSA網路故障後數分鐘，主要股價指數便跌至盤中低點；美債期貨成交量升至當日最高，現券殖利率則轉向盤中低檔。近期軟體、航空及金融服務已接連出現系統問題，蘋果服務也再傳故障。聯合航空表示，影響航班起飛的故障已解決；摩根大通也表示，已修復導致部分客戶週一交易延遲的技術問題。

加拿大皇家銀行資本市場策略師Izaac Brook將股市急跌與美債買盤歸因於NSA消息，認為債市仍在近期就業、通膨及聯準會消息形成的區間內交易。TJM Institutional Services的David Robin則指出，科技系統故障與AI前景的不確定性，正促使資金轉向避險。盤中風險偏好轉變是這波行情的直接催化因素，早上消費數據即使未轉弱，也能出現這類避險買盤。

各天期美債普遍回升，中短天期表現略優於長端。5年期殖利率下降2.53個基點至4.9147%，30年期下降1.61個基點至5.458%。2年與10年期利差僅擴大0.1個基點至30.27個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大0.92個基點至65.39個基點。主要變化是整體殖利率水準下降，曲線僅小幅陡峭化。

放到較長期間比較，借款成本仍然較高。10年期殖利率較11月10日高11.72個基點，較10月16日高3.4個基點；2年期較一週前及一個月前分別上升6.64與9.58個基點，30年期較一週前上升10.56個基點。週二漲勢只收復近期調整的一部分，10年期殖利率仍在5%以上。

當日支撐來自實質殖利率。10年期抗通膨公債（TIPS）殖利率下降3.62個基點至2.8792%，損益兩平通膨率則上升1.19個基點至2.2276%。與一週前相比，實質殖利率仍高10.89個基點，損益兩平通膨率高0.83個基點；與一個月前相比，實質殖利率上升15.72個基點，通膨補償下降12.32個基點。因此，當日名目公債上漲反映實質折現率降低，同時伴隨通膨補償略增。

油價帶來的助力不如週一。布蘭特期油上漲0.68%至每桶$93.07，西德州原油下跌0.13%至$85.61。中東再起戰事及航運遇襲，與供給前景較充裕的因素相互拉鋸。路透報導，懸掛巴拿馬旗的液化石油氣輪Tara Gas在阿曼海塞卜附近遭投射物擊中起火，24名船員全數撤離。印度外交部表示，攻擊發生於11月16日，兩名船員住院；撤離消息於11月17日傳出。攻擊者身份與完整損害程度仍不明。

伊朗國會議長Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf威脅，若伊朗同類民用設施遭到攻擊，將報復美國或以色列基地附近的民用基礎設施。其後梅爾通訊社報導，美軍攻擊格什姆島，未造成人員傷亡或民用基礎設施損壞；一名美軍官員則稱，打擊目標是伊朗飛彈發射場。這項有條件的報復威脅及新一輪攻擊，持續增加能源安全的不確定性，兩大原油指標最終漲跌互見。

早上的貿易價格數據提供了更直接的通膨訊號。10月進口物價月增1.1%，與9月相同，高於路透調查經濟學家預估的0.7%；非燃料進口物價由月增0.5%加快至0.8%。資本財價格月增1.5%，創下該序列自1988年12月按月發布以來最大漲幅。美國勞工統計局列出的推升項目包括電腦、周邊設備、半導體、電氣設備，以及工業與服務業機械。

燃料進口價格月增3.6%，其中石油產品上漲3.7%，天然氣上漲5.1%。漲勢也涵蓋車輛、零件與引擎，月增0.4%，以及汽車以外的消費品，月增0.5%；食品、飼料及飲料則下降0.2%。出口物價月增1.1%，低於9月的2.4%，但高於經濟日曆預測的0.5%。這批貿易價格數據中，與資本支出相關的設備漲幅尤其突出。由於2025年政府停擺，去年同期部分資料未能蒐集，勞工統計局無法計算受影響項目的10月年增率。

其他經濟數據呈現明顯分化。ADP每週就業人數增加23,750人，前值為19,250人。Redbook銷售年增率由10.1%降至9.5%。9月企業庫存月增0.5%，符合預期，前值為0.4%；汽車以外的零售庫存月增0.5%，前值為0.1%。

10月工業生產月減0.4%，9月則增加0.7%，疲弱主要集中在製造業以外。公用事業產出下降4.3%，回吐9月4.4%增幅的大部分，礦業下降0.8%。製造業產出月增0.3%，與前月相同，高於當日經濟日曆預測的0.2%；但排除汽車及零件後，工廠產出下降0.1%。

企業設備產出月增1.0%、年增7.8%，消費品產出則月減0.7%。聯準會公布的工業生產總量較2025年10月增加2.1%。產能利用率由修正後的76.8%降至76.4%，低於維持不變的預期，也比1972至2025年平均低3個百分點。整體產出下滑之際，設備仍強，汽車以外的製造業則較弱。

住宅市場更清楚呈現高利率的代價。11月NAHB／富國銀行建商信心指數下跌4點至25，低於預期的29，創2012年4月以來最低。當前銷售指數下跌6點至28，銷售預期與潛在買家來客量各下降2點。四大地區信心全數轉弱，南部與西部降至逾十年低點。30年期房貸利率仍遠高於7%，46%的建商表示已降價，比例創疫情以來最高，68%採用促銷優惠。NAHB經濟學家Robert Dietz也將關稅推升建材成本、勞工短缺及法規，列為限制購屋負擔能力的因素。

聖路易聯準銀行總裁Musalem的主張相當具體。他在為阿根廷央行貨幣與銀行會議準備的談話中表示，實質政策利率可能需要在2027年春季前提高約1個百分點。他估計目前實質利率接近1.0%至1.5%區間的下緣，希望明確升至2.0%至2.5%區間。通膨超過3%、成長高於趨勢，而聯邦資金利率區間為3.75%至4%，在他看來政策限制性不足，可能必須主要透過直接升息加強緊縮。他認為及早行動，可降低最終恢復物價穩定對就業及經濟造成的代價。Musalem今年沒有投票權，下次排定的投票年度為2028年；若亞特蘭大聯準銀行總裁職位持續懸缺，他將在2027年取得投票權。

Williams在紐約Axios活動上，對行動速度提出不同看法。他表示經濟強勁且持續增強，通膨也居高不下，但不認為需要大幅行動，主張花時間分析新資訊。他未見價格壓力擴散，並認為關稅對通膨的大部分影響已經過去；AI則可能是較持久的通膨推力。若AI與其他成長動能延續，明年可能需要進一步升息。他認為金融情勢雖已稍微回歸正常，仍支撐成長。

期貨已完全反映12月升息25個基點，市場也認為1月及4月可能續升。Bloomberg當日報導顯示，至2027年9月的預期緊縮幅度超過80個基點。美國銀行Mark Cabana另預測，2年期美債殖利率年底將達5%，理由是目前利率尚未明顯限制經濟活動，而較高的短期殖利率可能帶動全球殖利率上升。這也呈現週二避險漲勢面臨的反向風險。

部位配置可能放大雙向反轉。美國銀行策略師表示，部分動能交易帳戶近期重建美債空頭部位，若避險需求再起，這些空頭便容易受壓。摩根大通截至11月16日當週的客戶調查則呈現另一面：純空頭部位持平在8月17日以來最低，多頭比例上升3個百分點，中性比例同步下降3個百分點。盤中快速上漲發生時，各類投資人的部位並不一致，並非普遍加碼看空。

美國財政部的長天期公債買回結果異常偏低：目標$60億，實際僅買回$11.8億，市場提交出售的債券也只有$45億。此前五次針對10至20年期或20至30年期債券的操作，均達最高買回額；前七次提交金額介於$105億至$464億。SMBC Capital Markets的Monty Gandhi認為，年底交易活動減少可能解釋這項結果，並可能影響餘下操作。當日市場早盤反轉後，到紐約時間下午1時40分至2時的操作時段已趨穩定。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack談的則是聯準會如何應對美債市場失靈。她主張，應以衝擊是否外溢至實體經濟設定較高的干預門檻，改善常設附買回機制的運作時段，並考慮將交割連結FedNow，讓資金可在上午8時前到位。若附買回操作不足，她支持考慮暫時、針對性的買債，搭配明確退場策略，且持有部位應與貨幣政策資產分開。這套架構將緊急市場支援與刺激措施區分開來，也容許基本面驅動的價格調整及波動持續發生。

## AI融資：個別專案風險與供給減少並存

Pimco最新的相對價值評估，將建設延誤列為AI信用前景的核心因素。截至11月10日，以大型雲端公司承租的資料中心為支持的投資級債券，利差比這些雲端公司直接發行的可比債券高約146個基點，9月底則接近180個基點。策略師Lotfi Karoui認為，許可審批趨嚴與建造成本提高，可能抑制發債，讓這項利差進一步收窄。

他預期建設期將拉長，進度也更不平順。市場對亞馬遜、Alphabet、Meta、微軟及甲骨文的支出共識估計，未來兩年每年均約$1.2兆。延誤將使部分融資需求分散到更長時間，減輕短期供給；運算容量較稀缺，也可能支撐既有設施的使用率及定價。Pimco較正面的看法，特別針對大型雲端業者支持的資料中心債券，著眼於其較寬利差及潛在稀缺性支撐。

對高槓桿基礎設施供應商，Pimco仍然審慎，因為工程延誤使營收遞延，利息、租賃及晶片採購承諾卻仍需負擔。Bloomberg報導，匯豐以面額百分之八十幾的中段價位，出售一筆與甲骨文相關的新墨西哥州園區貸款，金額約$3億。這筆貸款屬於Doña Ana郡開發案$180億融資方案的一部分。監管與領導層的不確定性促使銀行重新評估曝險，折價出售反映了市場對該專案及AI放款的疑慮。

另一筆大型融資可能很快測試需求。知情人士表示，SpaceX為採購AI晶片安排的$400億債務融資，部分最早可能本週開始銷售，由高盛與Apollo承銷。Atlas SP管理的特殊目的機構將購買輝達晶片並發行資產擔保證券，使借款不列入SpaceX資產負債表，並讓公司維持投資級評等。先前已私下接洽投資人，目前的新進展是可能啟動銷售。

Bloomberg的Odd Lots電子報引述報導指出，亞太資料中心公司自2023年以來已籌得約$490億貸款。這個融資規模，使美國最新遠端存取限制的影響超出中國AI公司股價，因為貸款償還取決於在建運算容量能否用於商業營運。在美國先前公布許可證措施後，北京最新警告，若華府推動限制，中國將採取報復，令領袖峰會前的政治回應升高。

輝達本身的新消息，則分別涉及領導層不確定性及產品需求。黃仁勳週二表示，若董事會認為符合公司利益，他願意回任執行長；董事會目前並未考慮讓他復職。輝達另成立董事會委員會，監督國家安全政策。《華爾街日報》報導，美國證券交易委員會正調查該公司。

美股收盤後，輝達預測會計年度第4季營收為$1,300億、上下浮動3%，高於分析師平均預估的$1,253億，帶動股價盤後上漲約2%。在正常交易時段連跌四天後，這項展望提供了較強的營運訊號，領導層與監管問題則仍待釐清。預測公布的時間晚於當日引發美債買盤的股市跌勢。

投資人對科技業的態度已明顯轉弱。美國銀行基金經理人調查顯示，科技股淨加碼比例由10月的37%降至12%，創2006年以來最大降幅。週二整體股市波動進一步升高，VIX上漲11.13%至25.46。半導體表現則有所區別，費城半導體指數上漲0.34%，那斯達克100下跌。整體信心退潮之中，科技業內部仍有差異。

## 槓桿借款人取得融資，違約預測同步上升

銀行推動CCC Intelligent Solutions收購債務銷售之際，融資報價明顯改善。知情人士表示，$22億、7年期B類定期貸款的利差最低降至基準利率加3.75個百分點，原先為加4.25個百分點；發行價格由最低面額的98%提高至99.5%。另一筆$6.5億高收益債券，討論殖利率由初步約9%降至8.75%，投資需求至少$70億。

貸款利差降低、發行價格提高，都使借款人的擬議條件改善。這筆$28.5億融資方案，支應GTCR與Elliott以$61億收購這家汽車保險軟體供應商，最快週二定價。銀行面臨年底前愈來愈短的銷售窗口，這筆特定軟體業融資仍吸引強勁需求。摩根大通也準備出售部分Qualtrics債務；數月前承銷銀行未能順利售出的相關債務超過$50億。

不過，摩根大通最新違約預測顯示，槓桿貸款將面臨更艱難的時期。分析師預期，貸款違約率將由10月的1.96%，升至2027年的4.5%及2028年的4.75%。高收益債券的預估較低，明年為2.75%、2028年為3%，今年10月底為2.63%。浮動利率的利息負擔，以及對軟體、資訊科技與建材產業較高的曝險，是貸款前景較弱的主要原因。

到期結構也增加壓力。該行指出，2027至2029年到期的$8,620億債務中，46%評等為B3或以下。若利率維持高檔，面臨產業結構問題與AI衝擊的借款人，再融資尤其困難；重整也可能改變清償順位，或移走既有貸款人原可依賴的擔保品。今年迄今，槓桿融資市場已發生17起違約，涉及金額近$300億，其中債券約$210億，其餘為貸款。摩根大通預測的是在這個現況之上進一步惡化。

Optimum Communications則有另一項重整進展。公司與債權人正討論，將相對於某項獲利指標的槓桿倍數，由約8倍降至約3倍，可能使約$260億債務削減超過一半。債權人於重整後取得的新債金額尚未確定；討論中的方案是由債權人取得至少90%的重整後股權，Patrick Drahi等股東保留其餘部分，摩根大通提供的一筆貸款則繼續存續。

此前，CSC Holdings週一決定不支付約$1.025億利息，利用30天寬限期協商。報導指出，Optimum持有現金約$11億，明年到期債務超過$60億。標普將評等降至CCC-，認為未來六個月很可能違約、進行困境換債或破產。依美國破產法第11章聲請重整，仍是落實將控制權移交貸款人的協議之可能途徑。

Tripadvisor則已完成償債。公司利用將TheFork出售給美國運通的所得，提前償還2031年到期、原額$8.34億定期貸款中的$6億。這筆貸款週一價格已上漲近11分至99分，償還消息於當日收盤後公布。按交易調整後的現金由$14億降至約$8億。公司減債之際，也正重整業務，並準備因應執行長Matt Goldberg於2月離任、財務長Michael Noonan於年底離職。Goldberg表示，整體重整措施按全年化計算可節省$4,000萬，為毛額估計。

歐洲私募股權業者也利用市場中需求較佳的部分籌資，但用途是提取現金，而非減債。Somacis擬發行€10.3億浮動利率債券，用於再融資及股東分配；Triton旗下MacGregor擬籌€6億，用於再融資及股利。Cahill Gordon & Reindel的Jeremy Duffy表示，接近年底，投資人熟悉的借款人可向既有投資人快速完成融資。銀行難以售出一筆€5.5億Aroma-Zone收購貸款，則顯示部分收購融資更具挑戰。市場偏好熟悉的信用，使股東分配融資仍能推進，同時其他已承銷交易持續占用銀行的銷售能力。

美國市政債供給的主要目的不同。巴克萊預測2027年發行量為$5,800億至$6,000億，略低於今年至少$6,000億的預估，市場規模到明年底將接近$5兆。高殖利率可能限制借新還舊，但基礎設施需求、偏高的建造與勞工成本、聯邦支援減少，以及近期通過的發債措施，均支撐新增資金借款。該行預期，機場工程及收費道路將帶動運輸類發行增加10%至15%，適用替代性最低稅的債券發行將增加5%至10%。醫療業借款可能包括收購融資，但借新還舊減少，預計仍會使該產業總發行量下降。

## 通膨使歐亞貨幣政策路徑分歧

澳洲央行會議紀錄揭示，2026年第五次升息背後存在分歧。六名成員支持11月將利率調升至4.85%，三名成員希望先花更多時間評估先前緊縮，以及經濟更劇烈下滑、失業上升的風險。多數成員認為，支出與投資具有韌性、通膨持續，緊縮不足的風險大於過度緊縮。

這項判斷背後的政策估計也有所變動。成員討論中性利率，以及與通膨穩定相容的失業率，是否高於先前估計。第3季整體與基礎通膨均超過8月預測，意外上行也涵蓋市場服務項目。幕僚預測，兩項通膨指標將到2027年底前仍高於3%，約2028年中才回到2%至3%目標區間的中點。

預測納入更強的產能壓力，以及衝突成本更大程度轉嫁的影響。理事會估計，石油與成品油價格自8月以來已上漲約20%至25%；幕僚假設新增衝突成本約三分之二會傳導至基礎通膨，但不確定性很大。資料中心投資支撐短期成長，較緊政策與住宅市場轉弱，則使2027年中起的成長展望下修。會議紀錄未暗示再度升息，多數經濟學家與交易員預期利率將暫時維持不變。副總裁Andrew Hauser另否認，自己先前公開談論通膨的說法，迫使理事會不得不升息。

日本央行前總裁黑田東彥提出另一種可能：若通膨問題更嚴重，利率可能需要超過中性水準。經濟學家對終端利率的預估中位數為1.75%，部分預估為2.5%，目前政策利率為1.25%。黑田認為近期經濟萎縮很可能只是暫時現象，並指出在失業率僅2.4%的經濟中，預定4月開始、為期兩年的食品消費稅減稅，可能推高價格。他引述的估計顯示，該措施將向經濟挹注約¥10兆。

知情人士則表示，日本財務省傾向延後原定1月推出的浮動利率公債。投資人預期只剩幾次升息，對可防範進一步升息的工具需求減弱。財務省雖已完成系統升級，仍將在6月發債檢討時重新評估，考慮2027會計年度或更晚推出。終端政策利率的討論之外，這項發債安排也反映投資人對該工具的需求。

紐西蘭最新通膨預期數據，進一步凸顯其相對利率劣勢。5年期通膨預期降至2023年第1季以來最低，推動紐幣一度跌至54.84美分。紐西蘭與美國10年期殖利率差前一週曾達負48個基點，為2019年12月以來最寬，隨後收窄至約負30個基點。紐西蘭銀行的Jason Wong將匯價疲弱，歸因於這項負利差及紐西蘭央行對緊縮的謹慎態度。

英國勞動數據顯示，受僱人數減少，薪資壓力仍相對穩固。10月薪資名冊受僱人數減少34,000人，市場原估增加10,000人；9月則上修為增加20,000人。截至9月的三個月，民間部門經常性薪資年增率維持3.1%，失業率降至4.6%。職缺降至690,000個，為排除疫情期間後2014年以來最低，18個產業中有11個招聘下降，弱勢集中在小型企業。英國國家統計局提醒，受訪樣本變動似乎影響了就業及失業估計。

家庭購買力也轉弱。9月經CPI調整的經常性薪資年減0.2%，為2023年5月以來首次下降，名目薪資仍年增3.5%。數據尚未明顯顯示能源成本引發第二輪薪資效應，但英國央行官員預期，明年初薪資協商時，這項風險會更清楚。施羅德David Rees認為，勞動市場仍足夠強勁，12月升息仍有可能，且終端利率可能超過他預測的4.5%。

散戶需求則為英國公債提供另一項支撐。Hargreaves Lansdown表示，10月英國公債交易量比1至9月月均高近60%，也接近2025年月均的兩倍。今年該平台買入量第二高的是2056年到期、票息5.375%的公債，10月到期債券資金再投資也帶動交易。這反映的是拋售期間逐漸形成的投資需求，並非新的政策訊號。

歐盟執委會將2026年歐元區成長預測由0.9%上修至1.2%，並預測2027年成長1.2%、2028年成長1.3%。與資料中心投資相關的出口，以及就業與薪資支持的消費，協助經濟承受能源衝擊。通膨預估今年3.2%、明年3.1%、2028年2.1%。借款成本上升預計壓抑住宅建設，生活成本也使消費轉弱。

法國在這份預測中格外突出。執委會預測今年赤字占GDP的5.5%，高於政府修正後5.4%的目標；2027年為5.4%，高於5%的目標。經濟成長預估今年僅0.4%、明年0.6%，利息支出增加抵銷財政整頓。債務占GDP比率預計由2025年的115.7%升至2028年的123.2%；若政策不變，2028年赤字將再度擴大至5.7%。預算措施面臨政治阻力，也限制進一步調整的空間。

歐洲央行接班協商亦有進展。知情人士表示，德國計畫提名普林斯頓大學經濟學家Markus Brunnermeier出任首席經濟學家，作為執政聯盟協議的一部分，預期可為支持Pablo Hernandez de Cos出任總裁鋪路；柏林內閣預定週三敲定方案。先前法德達成協議的報導曾遭否認，如今協商進入新階段，正式任命仍待完成。

## 新興市場融資與重整進展不一

匈牙利連續第三個月將政策利率維持5.5%，但重新打開12月降息的可能。央行總裁Mihaly Varga表示，本次表決並非全體一致，會中已討論降息；下次決策將考慮新預測、國際環境，以及匈牙利有利的風險評價能否維持。交易員先前已排除今年降息，調整對新指引的定價後，福林兌歐元下跌逾0.5%。

政府承諾採用歐元，以及提出的財政整頓計畫，是Varga評估中的重要因素。10月通膨加快至2%，仍低於近期調降、2028年起適用的2.5%目標。他表示，油價偏高與市場波動仍要求審慎。穆迪預定週五檢視匈牙利主權評等，三大評等機構預計均將於年底前完成評估。

安哥拉則已降息，將基準利率調降75個基點至14%，連續第四次下調，降至逾十年最低。通膨由去年底15.7%降至10月8.16%，央行預期年底將接近7.5%至9.5%預測區間的下緣。央行維持約6%的成長預測，非石油經濟活動成長約7%。在許多非洲國家仍承受能源成本、匯率及聯準會前景壓力之際，安哥拉國內通膨降溫使其得以寬鬆。

哥倫比亞最新經濟數據則呈現較棘手的組合。第3季GDP年增僅0.5%，低於預測中位數1%，較前季萎縮0.8%。礦業成長7.8%、公用事業成長3.9%，農業萎縮6.7%、製造業萎縮1.2%。報導將疲弱歸因於地震及高利率。通膨加快下，央行今年已累計升息3個百分點至12.25%，經濟學家不預期未來幾個月降息。國會正審議財政救援法案，希望將明年赤字控制在GDP的9%以下。

阿根廷能源借款人的融資評估則較正面。桑坦德預測，2027年企業及省政府美元發行量約$90億，今年迄今已超過$110億；為避開10月總統大選，發行將集中上半年。其投資銀行主管Mariano Urquiola表示，儘管市況波動，體質較強的能源公司仍可用個位數殖利率借款。企業與省政府自2024年以來累計發行近$300億，這波重返市場並非由聯邦政府帶動。

待辦融資包括桑坦德及摩根大通牽頭、計畫規模$140億至$150億的Argentina LNG融資，以及涉及Transportadora de Gas del Sur與Pampa Energia的天然氣液體專案融資工作。明年主權償債金額將增至約$250億，這些專案支撐未來外匯流入。桑坦德預期，境外融資窗口愈難掌握，國內美元連結債券發行將增加。阿根廷政府美元債10月下跌近6%，也凸顯較強出口商與主權信用的差異。

新世界發展增資的新細節，釐清股權籌資與貸款展期的連動。執行長黃少媚表示，銀行將HK$738億貸款展延兩年的條件，是供股完成；增資與再融資互為條件。CreditSights的Zerlina Zeng認為，即使鄭氏家族計畫投入資金，讓債券持有人對股東支持較為放心，落實方案的風險仍高。10月將近期到期美元票據換成2032年到期、票息7.375%擔保債券的方案，最高擬交換$6億，實際獲提交$1.993億，顯示新股權計畫提出前，自願債權人參與仍有限。

中國公債在最新月度持倉資料中獲得外資加碼。中債登資料顯示，10月境外持有額增加人民幣395億元至2.08兆元，連續第六個月增加，也是5月以來最大增額。法國興業銀行Kiyong Seong將需求歸因於全球債市波動之際，中國公債相對穩定；他預期成長疲弱將支持殖利率下滑，人民銀行不時介入則會抑制漲勢。這些數字反映10月資金配置，與最近一日交易有別。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，委內瑞拉國民議會將最高新增借款$266億的法案送交委員會審議，之後才進行最終逐條表決。草案為公共投資專案簽約及其他專案融資撥款各編列11.6兆玻利瓦，另編列1.18兆玻利瓦，用於再融資或重整。反對派議員Julio Cesar Reyes在首次表決未予支持，反對審議時間過短，並要求精確交代公共債務情況。這是政府推動重整期間，借款授權法案的最新審議進展。

## 後續市場焦點

美國10月住宅建設數據將於11月18日美東時間上午8時30分公布。在建商普遍降價並提供優惠、11月信心再度惡化之際，這項數據將呈現實際建築活動。11月19日上午10時公布的第3季服務業預先報告，將把需求觀察從零售支出及工廠產出擴展至其他領域。11月20日各州就業數據將補充勞動市場的地區細節；11月25日10月耐久財訂單，則將在企業設備產出及資本財進口價格強勁之後，再提供一項投資需求訊號。

Anthropic於11月18日的首次公開發行定價，仍是一項獨立而重大的融資考驗。公司引導投資人朝每股$70至$78區間頂端或以上出價，若定在$78，完全稀釋估值約$1.4兆。訂單包含多筆至少$100億的認購意向，預計週四開始交易。若這些認購需求落實為完成發行的股權募資，將與輝達較強的營收預測，以及SpaceX晶片擔保債務可能啟動銷售的進展，一同影響AI產業不同領域的融資信心。

澳洲週三薪資及週四就業數據，將協助判斷澳洲央行的通膨疑慮，與少數成員警告的更劇烈衰退風險如何交互影響。英國週三CPI預計顯示通膨為3.6%，在受僱人數減少、實質薪資下降、民間薪資成長仍穩的背景下，提供新的價格資訊。匈牙利12月預測將決定週二討論的降息選項能否落實，週五穆迪評等檢視則先行測試該國風險評價。

柏林內閣預計週三、也就是提名截止日，決定歐洲央行人事方案。在執委會預測通膨持續、法國債務比率惡化之際，擬議的首席經濟學家任命及總裁人選支持，將確立領導層交接的下一階段。正式政治協議仍待達成。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries reversed early losses as another wave of technology disruptions drove investors toward government debt, overcoming the initial pressure from stronger U.S. consumer spending. The 10-year yield fell 2.43 basis points to 5.1068%, while the two-year declined 2.53 basis points to 4.8041%. Falling real yields accounted for the recovery as inflation compensation edged higher, leaving a different combination from the previous session's oil-led relief.

The haven bid gathered force after a reported outage at a National Security Agency communications network compounded unease about technology companies and the AI investment boom. The S&P 500 lost 1.03% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.72%. Those losses coexisted with a Federal Reserve debate increasingly focused on how quickly to raise rates: Alberto Musalem advocated several increases before spring, while John Williams rejected the need for an outsized move and made further tightening dependent in part on the persistence of AI-driven growth.

Financing markets continued to distinguish among borrowers. Pimco argued that slower data-center construction could improve the relative pricing of bonds backed by major cloud tenants, even as a discounted bank-loan sale exposed concern about an individual development. Banks tightened terms on CCC Intelligent Solutions' buyout financing, while JPMorgan forecast a marked increase in leveraged-loan defaults. The session paired renewed demand for Treasury protection with continuing access to capital for selected credits, against a backdrop of rising imported costs and increasingly visible pressure on housing.

## Treasury Reversal Meets Stronger Spending and Higher Import Costs

The Treasury rally developed after October retail sales initially pushed yields higher. The most important demand signal was the control group, which increased 0.6% against a 0.4% forecast and a previous 0.5%, according to the dated AMP economic calendar. Headline sales rose 0.2%, matching expectations but slowing from 0.8%. The composition gave the market a stronger underlying consumption reading than the headline slowdown alone suggested.

By late morning, the sequence changed. Bloomberg reported that equity benchmarks fell to session lows within minutes of CNN's account of an NSA network outage. Treasury futures volumes reached their highest level of the day as cash yields reversed toward session lows. The disruptions followed recent failures affecting software, airlines and financial services; fresh problems also hit Apple services. United Airlines said it had resolved an outage affecting departures, and JPMorgan said it had fixed the technical issue that delayed some customer transactions Monday.

RBC Capital Markets strategist Izaac Brook attributed the abrupt equity decline and Treasury bid to the NSA headlines, describing the bond move as trading within the range established by recent employment, inflation and Fed news. TJM Institutional Services' David Robin said uncertainty over technology breakdowns and the AI outlook was generating a flight to safety. Neither assessment required a deterioration in the morning's consumption figures: the immediate catalyst was a change in risk appetite during the session.

The recovery was broad but modestly stronger before the long end. Five-year yields fell 2.53 basis points to 4.9147%, while the 30-year declined 1.61 basis points to 5.458%. The two- to 10-year spread widened just 0.1 basis point to 30.27 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap increased 0.92 basis point to 65.39. This was principally a decline in the level of yields, with only limited curve steepening.

The broader comparison still showed higher borrowing costs. The 10-year yield was 11.72 basis points above November 10 and 3.4 basis points above October 16. Two-year yields were up 6.64 basis points over the week and 9.58 over the month; the 30-year was 10.56 basis points higher over the week. Tuesday's gains reduced part of the recent adjustment without taking the benchmark below 5%.

Real yields provided the day's relief. The 10-year TIPS yield declined 3.62 basis points to 2.8792%, while the breakeven increased 1.19 basis points to 2.2276%. Over the week, the real yield remained 10.89 basis points higher and the breakeven was up 0.83; over the month, real yields had increased 15.72 basis points while inflation compensation fell 12.32. The daily nominal rally therefore came through a lower real discount rate, with a small increase in the compensation for inflation.

Oil offered less help than on Monday. Brent futures rose 0.68% to $93.07 a barrel, while WTI slipped 0.13% to $85.61. Renewed fighting and shipping attacks in the Middle East competed with a more comfortable supply outlook. Reuters reported the evacuation of all 24 crew from the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas after a projectile strike and fire near Khasab, Oman. India's foreign ministry dated the attack to November 16 and said two crew members were hospitalized; the evacuation was reported November 17. The attacker and full extent of the damage remained unclear.

Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf threatened retaliation against civilian infrastructure near U.S. or Israeli bases if comparable Iranian sites were attacked. Mehr subsequently reported U.S. strikes on Qeshm Island without casualties or damage to civilian infrastructure; a U.S. military official described a strike on an Iranian missile launch site. The conditional threat and renewed strikes sustained uncertainty over energy security while crude benchmarks finished in different directions.

The morning's trade-price release supplied a more direct inflation signal. October import prices rose 1.1%, matching September's increase and exceeding the 0.7% economist consensus reported by Reuters. Nonfuel import prices accelerated to 0.8% from 0.5%. Capital-goods prices increased 1.5%, the largest monthly rise since that series began monthly publication in December 1988, with computers, peripherals, semiconductors, electrical apparatus and industrial and service machinery among the drivers identified by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Fuel import prices rose 3.6%, including increases of 3.7% for petroleum products and 5.1% for natural gas. The breadth extended to vehicles, parts and engines, up 0.4%, and consumer goods excluding autos, up 0.5%; foods, feeds and beverages fell 0.2%. Export prices increased 1.1%, down from September's 2.4% but above the calendar's 0.5% forecast. These were trade-price observations, with particularly strong increases in equipment relevant to capital spending. BLS could not calculate affected October annual comparisons because the 2025 government shutdown had prevented collection of the year-earlier observations.

Other releases showed considerable dispersion within activity. Weekly ADP employment increased 23,750, compared with 19,250 previously. Redbook's annual sales growth slowed to 9.5% from 10.1%. September business inventories rose 0.5%, matching expectations after 0.4%, while retail inventories excluding autos increased 0.5% after 0.1%.

Industrial production fell 0.4% in October after a 0.7% September increase, with the weakness concentrated outside manufacturing. Utilities output dropped 4.3%, reversing much of September's 4.4% gain, and mining fell 0.8%. Manufacturing rose 0.3%, matching the previous month's gain and exceeding the dated calendar's 0.2% forecast. Excluding motor vehicles and parts, however, factory output slipped 0.1%.

Business-equipment production increased 1.0% monthly and 7.8% annually, while consumer-goods output declined 0.7% monthly. Total industrial production was 2.1% above October 2025 in the Fed's release. Capacity utilization fell to 76.4% from a revised 76.8%, against expectations for no change, and stood 3 percentage points below its 1972-2025 average. The aggregate contraction thus accompanied continued equipment strength and a softer manufacturing result beyond autos.

Housing supplied a clearer sign of the cost of high rates. The NAHB/Wells Fargo builder-sentiment index fell 4 points to 25 in November, against expectations for 29, reaching its lowest level since April 2012. Present sales dropped 6 points to 28, while sales expectations and prospective-buyer traffic each declined 2 points. Sentiment weakened in all four regions, with the South and West at their lowest levels in more than a decade. With 30-year mortgage rates still well above 7%, 46% of builders reported cutting prices, the largest share since the pandemic, and 68% used sales incentives. NAHB economist Robert Dietz also identified tariff-related materials costs, labor shortages and regulation as affordability constraints.

Musalem's prescription was more forceful than a general call for restraint. In remarks for the Central Bank of Argentina's Money and Banking Conference, the St. Louis Fed president said the real policy rate might need to rise about 1 percentage point before spring 2027. He put the current real rate near the lower end of 1.0%-1.5% and wanted it solidly within 2.0%-2.5%. With inflation above 3%, growth above trend and the federal funds range at 3.75%-4%, he judged policy insufficiently restrictive and argued that direct rate increases might have to do most of the work. Earlier action, in his assessment, could reduce the eventual employment and economic cost of restoring price stability. Musalem does not vote this year; his next scheduled vote is in 2028, although he would vote in 2027 if the Atlanta presidency remains vacant.

Williams offered a different judgment on pace at an Axios event in New York. He said the economy was strong and strengthening and inflation remained stubbornly high, but rejected the suggestion that conditions called for dramatic action. He supported taking time to analyze incoming information, said he was not seeing a broadening of price pressures and considered most tariff effects on inflation behind the economy. AI was a potentially more persistent inflation driver, he said; continued strength from AI and other growth forces could require more increases next year. Financial conditions had normalized somewhat but still supported growth in his assessment.

Futures fully priced a quarter-point December increase, with further moves in January and April seen as likely. Bloomberg's session account put expected tightening by September 2027 at more than 80 basis points. Bank of America's Mark Cabana separately forecast a two-year Treasury yield of 5% by year-end, arguing that rates were not materially constraining activity and that higher short-term yields could pull global yields upward. That forecast identifies the risk on the other side of Tuesday's haven rally.

Positioning could amplify reversals in either direction. Bank of America strategists said some momentum accounts had recently rebuilt bearish Treasury positions, leaving shorts vulnerable to renewed safety demand. JPMorgan's client survey for the week through November 16 showed a different part of the picture: outright shorts were unchanged at their lowest since August 17, while longs increased 3 percentage points as neutrals declined by the same amount. The rapid intraday rally occurred against an uneven positioning backdrop rather than a uniform increase in bearish exposure.

Treasury's own operation produced an unusually small result. Its long-dated buyback purchased $1.18 billion against a $6 billion target, with participants offering only $4.5 billion. Each of the previous five operations targeting 10- to 20-year or 20- to 30-year debt had reached the maximum; offers in the previous seven operations ranged from $10.5 billion to $46.4 billion. SMBC Capital Markets' Monty Gandhi suggested year-end reductions in activity could explain the result and affect the remaining operations. The market had stabilized by the 1:40-2 p.m. New York operation window after its earlier reversal.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack addressed a separate question: how the Fed should respond to Treasury-market dysfunction. She proposed a high intervention threshold tied to spillovers into the real economy, improvements to the Standing Repo Facility's operating hours and possible settlement links to FedNow that could provide liquidity before 8 a.m. If repo proved insufficient, she supported considering temporary, targeted purchases with a clear exit strategy and a portfolio distinct from monetary-policy holdings. Her framework would distinguish emergency market support from stimulus, while allowing fundamental repricing and volatility to proceed without intervention.

## AI Financing Splits Between Project Risk and Scarcer Supply

Pimco's new relative-value assessment put construction delays at the center of the AI credit outlook. As of November 10, investment-grade bonds backed by data centers leased to major cloud companies traded about 146 basis points wider than comparable debt issued directly by those companies, compared with close to 180 basis points in late September. Strategist Lotfi Karoui argued that tighter permits and higher construction costs could curb issuance and narrow that gap further.

His expectation was for a longer, less linear buildout. Consensus spending estimates for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle were around $1.2 trillion in each of the next two years. Delays would spread part of those financing requirements over a longer period, easing near-term supply. Scarcer computing capacity could also support utilization and pricing for existing facilities. Pimco's more favorable view was specifically directed at hyperscaler-backed data-center bonds, with their wider spreads and potential scarcity support.

The firm remained cautious about leveraged infrastructure providers whose interest, leases and chip-purchase commitments continue while construction setbacks delay revenues. That distinction became tangible in Bloomberg's reporting that HSBC sold roughly $300 million of a loan for an Oracle-linked New Mexico campus at prices in the mid-80s. The slice belonged to an $18 billion financing package for the Doña Ana County development. The discounted disposal reflected concern surrounding that project and AI lending as banks reassessed exposures amid regulatory and leadership uncertainty.

Another large structure may soon test demand. Part of the $40 billion debt financing for SpaceX's AI-chip purchases could begin selling as soon as this week, according to a person familiar with the transaction. Goldman Sachs and Apollo are underwriting the expected deal. An Atlas SP-managed special-purpose vehicle would purchase Nvidia chips and issue asset-backed securities, keeping the borrowing off SpaceX's balance sheet and allowing it to maintain investment-grade ratings. The current development is the possible start of distribution after earlier private investor discussions.

Across Asia Pacific, Bloomberg reporting cited in the Odd Lots newsletter put loans raised by data-center companies since 2023 at about $49 billion. That financing base gives the new U.S. remote-access restrictions significance beyond the share prices of Chinese AI companies: repayment depends on the commercial use of the computing capacity being built. The latest warning from Beijing said China would retaliate if Washington proceeds with the restrictions. It sharpened the political response ahead of the leaders' summit, following the previously announced U.S. licensing initiative.

Nvidia's own fresh developments separated leadership uncertainty from demand for its products. Jensen Huang said Tuesday that he would return as CEO if the board decided that was in the company's interests; the board was not considering reinstatement. Nvidia also established a board committee to oversee national-security policy. The Wall Street Journal reported an SEC investigation of the company.

After the U.S. equity close, Nvidia forecast fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above the $125.3 billion analyst average. Its shares rose about 2% in late trading. The outlook supplied a stronger operating signal after a fourth consecutive regular-session decline, while the leadership and regulatory questions remained open. The forecast arrived after the equity selloff that had generated the day's Treasury demand.

Investor attitudes toward the sector had weakened sharply. Bank of America's fund-manager survey showed the net share overweight technology falling to 12% from 37% in October, the largest decline since 2006. Broad equity volatility rose further Tuesday: the VIX increased 11.13% to 25.46. Semiconductor performance was more differentiated, with the PHLX index gaining 0.34% even as the Nasdaq 100 declined. Those observations capture a retreat in aggregate confidence alongside variation within the technology complex.

## Leveraged Borrowers Secure Deals as Default Forecasts Rise

CCC Intelligent Solutions obtained substantially improved financing indications as banks worked to distribute its buyout debt. The $2.2 billion seven-year term loan B was offered at a margin as low as 3.75 percentage points over the benchmark, down from 4.25 points, and at 99.5 cents on the dollar rather than as low as 98. The separate $650 million high-yield bond was discussed at an 8.75% yield against initial talk around 9%, with at least $7 billion of investor interest, people familiar with the transaction said.

The margin reduction and higher issue price both improved the proposed loan terms for the borrower. The $2.85 billion package backs GTCR and Elliott's $6.1 billion acquisition of the car-insurance software provider and could price as soon as Tuesday. Its reception showed strong demand for this particular software financing as banks faced a narrowing year-end distribution window. JPMorgan was also preparing to sell some of the more than $5 billion of Qualtrics debt that underwriters had been left holding months earlier.

JPMorgan's new default forecast nevertheless projected a more difficult period for leveraged loans. Its analysts expected the default rate to reach 4.5% in 2027 and 4.75% in 2028, from 1.96% in October. Their high-yield bond forecasts were lower: 2.75% next year and 3% in 2028, against 2.63% at October-end. Floating-rate interest burdens and greater exposure to software, information technology and building products were central to the weaker loan outlook.

The maturity profile adds pressure. Debt rated B3 or lower accounts for 46% of the $862 billion maturing from 2027 through 2029, according to the bank. Borrowers facing structural industry problems and AI disruption could find refinancing especially difficult if rates stay high. Restructurings may also alter the order of repayment or remove collateral available to existing lenders. So far this year, 17 defaults have involved almost $30 billion across leveraged finance, about $21 billion in bonds and the remainder in loans. The forecast concerns a future deterioration from that current experience.

Optimum Communications supplied a distinct restructuring development. Creditors and the company were discussing reducing leverage to about three times a measure of earnings from roughly eight times, potentially cutting its approximately $26 billion debt pile by more than half. The proposed take-back debt amount remained unsettled. Creditors were discussing at least 90% of the reorganized equity, leaving shareholders including Patrick Drahi with the balance, while a JPMorgan-provided loan would remain outstanding under the proposal.

The talks followed CSC Holdings' decision to skip about $102.5 million of interest Monday and use a 30-day grace period to negotiate. Optimum had approximately $1.1 billion of cash, according to the reporting, and more than $6 billion of debt due next year. S&P cut its rating to CCC-, seeing default, a distressed exchange or bankruptcy as likely within six months. A possible Chapter 11 filing remained one route to implementing a deal that would transfer control to lenders.

Tripadvisor moved in the opposite direction through a completed repayment. It prepaid $600 million of its $834 million term loan due 2031 using proceeds from the sale of TheFork to American Express. The loan had climbed nearly 11 cents to 99 on Monday before the payment was announced after that session's close. Pro-forma cash declined from $1.4 billion to about $800 million. The reduction in debt arrived as the company reorganized its businesses and prepared for CEO Matt Goldberg's February departure and CFO Michael Noonan's exit at year-end. Goldberg said the broader restructuring would yield $40 million in gross annualized savings.

European sponsors were also using receptive pockets of the market, but to extract cash rather than reduce debt. Somacis sought €1.03 billion of floating-rate bonds for refinancing and a shareholder distribution; Triton-owned MacGregor sought €600 million for refinancing and a dividend. Cahill Gordon & Reindel's Jeremy Duffy said familiar borrowers could execute quickly with existing investors as year-end approached. Banks' difficulty placing a €550 million Aroma-Zone buyout loan illustrated the greater challenge for some acquisition financings. The preference for known credits was allowing distributions to proceed even as other underwritten deals strained distribution capacity.

Municipal supply has a different underlying purpose. Barclays forecast $580 billion-$600 billion of issuance in 2027, slightly below its expectation of at least $600 billion this year, with market size approaching $5 trillion by next year-end. High yields could constrain refundings, while infrastructure needs, elevated construction and labor costs, reduced federal support and recently approved bond measures support new-money borrowing. The bank expected transportation issuance to rise 10%-15% through airport work and toll roads, and alternative-minimum-tax issuance to grow 5%-10%. Healthcare borrowing could include acquisition finance, although lower refundings were expected to reduce that sector's overall total.

## Inflation Divides Policy Paths Across Europe and Asia

The Reserve Bank of Australia's minutes revealed the disagreement behind its fifth increase of 2026. Six members backed the November rise to 4.85%, while three wanted more time to assess earlier tightening and the risk of a sharper downturn and higher unemployment. The majority judged the danger of insufficient restraint greater than the risk of doing too much, citing resilient spending and investment alongside persistent inflation.

The policy estimates underlying that judgment had shifted. Members considered whether neutral interest rates and the unemployment rate consistent with stable inflation were higher than previously thought. September-quarter headline and underlying inflation exceeded August forecasts, with the surprise extending into market services. Staff projected both measures above 3% until late 2027 and a return to the midpoint of the 2%-3% target around mid-2028.

The forecasts included stronger capacity pressure and greater conflict-related cost pass-through. Oil and refined products had risen about 20%-25% since August in the board's assessment, and staff assumed roughly two-thirds of additional conflict costs would reach underlying inflation, with substantial uncertainty. Data-center investment supported near-term growth, while tighter policy and weaker housing reduced the outlook from mid-2027. The minutes did not signal another increase, and most economists and traders expected a period on hold. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser had separately rejected suggestions his earlier public inflation comments had boxed the board into tightening.

Former BOJ Governor Haruhiko Kuroda raised a different possibility for Japan: rates might need to exceed neutral if inflation became more serious. Economists' median terminal-rate estimate was 1.75%, with some seeing 2.5%, against a current policy rate of 1.25%. Kuroda regarded the recent contraction as probably temporary and argued that a planned two-year food sales-tax reduction beginning in April could push up prices in an economy with unemployment of 2.4%. The measure would add around ¥10 trillion to the economy in the assessment he cited. His view was conditional advice from a former governor.

Japan's Finance Ministry, meanwhile, was leaning toward delaying a floating-rate government-bond launch initially planned for January, according to people familiar with the matter. Demand for protection against further increases had weakened as investors anticipated only a few remaining hikes. The ministry would revisit the proposal at its June issuance review and assess a launch in fiscal 2027 or later, despite already completing system upgrades. The issuance decision reflects investor demand for the instrument alongside the debate over the eventual policy ceiling.

New Zealand's latest inflation-expectations observation reinforced its relative-rate disadvantage. Five-year expectations fell to their lowest since Q1 2023, helping push the kiwi as low as 54.84 U.S. cents. The gap between New Zealand and U.S. 10-year yields had reached minus 48 basis points the previous week, its widest since December 2019, before narrowing to around minus 30. BNZ's Jason Wong linked currency weakness to that negative differential and the RBNZ's caution over tightening.

Britain's labor figures showed weaker payrolls alongside relatively firm wage pressure. Payrolled employment fell 34,000 in October against expectations for a 10,000 increase, after an upwardly revised September gain of 20,000. Regular private-sector wage growth held at 3.1% in the three months through September and unemployment fell to 4.6%. Vacancies declined to 690,000, the lowest since 2014 outside the pandemic, with hiring falling in 11 of 18 sectors and weakness concentrated in small businesses. The ONS cautioned that a change in the respondent sample appeared to affect employment and unemployment estimates.

Household purchasing power weakened separately. Regular pay adjusted for CPI fell 0.2% annually in September, the first decline since May 2023, while nominal wages were still growing 3.5%. The release provided little evidence yet of energy costs generating second-round wage effects, but BOE officials expected the risk to become clearer in negotiations early next year. Schroders' David Rees judged the labor market sufficiently strong to keep December tightening in play and saw a risk of exceeding his 4.5% peak-rate forecast.

Retail demand was providing a distinct source of support for gilts. Hargreaves Lansdown said October gilt trades were almost 60% above the January-September monthly average and nearly double the 2025 average. Its second-most-purchased gilt this year was the 2056 bond, carrying a 5.375% coupon, with reinvestment of maturing October debt contributing to activity. The data describe investor demand developing through the selloff rather than a new policy signal.

The European Commission upgraded euro-area growth for 2026 to 1.2% from 0.9% and projected 1.2% in 2027 and 1.3% in 2028. Exports associated with data-center investment and consumption supported by employment and wages helped the economy withstand the energy shock. Inflation was projected at 3.2% this year, 3.1% next year and 2.1% in 2028. Higher borrowing costs were expected to weigh on housing construction as living costs softened consumption.

France stood apart within that forecast. The Commission projected a 5.5%-of-GDP deficit this year against the government's revised 5.4% target, and 5.4% in 2027 against a 5% goal. Growth was forecast at only 0.4% this year and 0.6% next year, with rising interest payments offsetting consolidation. Debt was expected to reach 123.2% of GDP in 2028 from 115.7% in 2025; without policy changes, the deficit would widen again to 5.7% in 2028. Political resistance to budget measures limits the room for further correction.

ECB succession talks also advanced. Germany planned to nominate Princeton economist Markus Brunnermeier for the chief-economist position as part of a coalition agreement expected to clear the way for support of Pablo Hernandez de Cos as president. Berlin's cabinet was due to seal the package Wednesday, according to people familiar with the negotiations. The development moves beyond earlier, denied reports of a Franco-German agreement, while leaving the formal appointments pending.

## Emerging-Market Funding and Restructuring Advance Unevenly

Hungary held its policy rate at 5.5% for a third month but reopened the possibility of easing in December. Governor Mihaly Varga said the vote was not unanimous and a cut had already been considered. Fresh forecasts, the international environment and persistence of the country's favorable risk assessment would inform the next decision. The forint fell more than 0.5% against the euro as traders adjusted to guidance after pricing out cuts for this year.

The government’s euro-adoption commitment and proposed fiscal consolidation were important to Varga's assessment. October inflation had accelerated to 2% but remained below the recently lowered 2.5% target effective from 2028. Elevated oil and volatile markets still warranted caution, he said. Moody's was scheduled to review the sovereign Friday, with all three major rating agencies expected to assess it by year-end.

Angola delivered an actual cut, lowering its benchmark 75 basis points to 14%, the fourth consecutive reduction and the lowest rate in more than a decade. Inflation had slowed to 8.16% in October from 15.7% at the end of last year, and the central bank expected it near the bottom of its 7.5%-9.5% year-end forecast range. It maintained a growth forecast around 6%, with non-oil activity expanding about 7%. That domestic disinflation allowed easing while many African peers faced pressure from energy costs, currencies and the Fed outlook.

Colombia's new activity release showed a more difficult combination. Q3 GDP rose just 0.5% annually against a 1% median forecast and fell 0.8% from the previous quarter. Mining grew 7.8% and utilities 3.9%, while agriculture contracted 6.7% and manufacturing 1.2%. The report attributed weakness to an earthquake and high interest rates. With the central bank having raised its rate 3 percentage points this year to 12.25% as inflation accelerated, economists did not expect cuts in the coming months. Congress was considering a fiscal rescue bill intended to keep next year's deficit below 9% of GDP.

Argentina's energy borrowers retained a more favorable financing assessment. Santander projected about $9 billion of corporate and provincial dollar issuance in 2027, compared with more than $11 billion so far this year, with sales concentrated in the first half ahead of October's presidential election. Its investment-banking head Mariano Urquiola said stronger energy companies could still borrow at single-digit yields despite volatile conditions. Corporate and provincial issuance has totaled almost $30 billion since 2024; the federal government has not driven this reopening.

The pipeline includes a planned $14 billion-$15 billion financing for Argentina LNG led by Santander and JPMorgan, alongside financing work for a natural-gas-liquids project involving Transportadora de Gas del Sur and Pampa Energia. These projects underpin prospective foreign-currency inflows as sovereign repayments rise to about $25 billion next year. Santander expected more domestic dollar-linked issuance as offshore windows become less predictable. The distinction between stronger exporters and the sovereign remained visible after Argentine government dollar bonds lost nearly 6% in October.

New details of New World Development's recapitalization clarified the connection between equity and loan relief. CEO Echo Huang said completion of the rights issue was a condition for banks extending HK$73.8 billion of loans by two years; the capital raising and refinancing were interconditional. CreditSights' Zerlina Zeng said execution risk remained high even as the Cheng family's planned contribution reassured bondholders about shareholder support. The October exchange of near-term dollar notes into 7.375% secured bonds due 2032 attracted $199.3 million of tenders against an offer for as much as $600 million, illustrating the limits of voluntary creditor participation before the new equity plan.

China's government bonds attracted fresh foreign allocations in the latest monthly holdings data. Overseas holdings rose 39.5 billion yuan in October to 2.08 trillion yuan, the sixth consecutive increase and the largest addition since May, according to Chinabond. Societe Generale's Kiyong Seong attributed demand to relative stability amid global bond volatility and expected weak growth to support lower yields, with periodic PBOC intervention moderating the rally. The figures describe October allocations, distinct from the latest day's trading.

After the U.S. fixed-income close, Venezuela's National Assembly advanced a bill allowing as much as $26.6 billion of additional borrowing to committee review before a final article-by-article vote. The draft allocated 11.6 trillion bolivars each to contracting public-investment projects and disbursing financing for other projects, plus 1.18 trillion bolivars for refinancing or restructuring. Opposition lawmaker Julio Cesar Reyes withheld support at the first vote, objecting to the limited review time and calling for a precise accounting of public debt. The new legislative step concerns borrowing authorization as the government pursues restructuring; the final vote remains ahead.

## Forward Market Significance

October U.S. residential construction is due November 18 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. The release will show activity behind November's renewed deterioration in builder sentiment, with price cuts and incentives already widespread. The Q3 Advance Services Report on November 19 at 10 a.m. will broaden the demand picture beyond retail spending and factory output. State employment data on November 20 will add regional detail to the labor assessment, while October durable-goods orders on November 25 will provide another observation of investment demand after strong business-equipment production and capital-goods import inflation.

Anthropic's November 18 IPO pricing remains a large independent funding test. The company was guiding investors toward the top of its $70-$78 range or above; $78 would imply a fully diluted valuation around $1.4 trillion. Orders included multiple indications of $10 billion or more, and trading was expected to begin Thursday. Converting that demand into a completed offering would bring a fresh equity-funding result alongside Nvidia's stronger revenue forecast and the prospective start of SpaceX's chip-backed debt distribution. Their outcomes will bear on financing confidence across different parts of the AI industry.

Australia's wage data Wednesday and employment report Thursday will help determine how the RBA's inflation concerns interact with the dissenters' warning of a sharper downturn. Britain's Wednesday CPI is expected to show inflation at 3.6%, putting a new price observation beside weaker payrolls, falling real pay and still-firm private wage growth. Hungary's December forecast round will determine whether the easing option discussed Tuesday becomes actionable, with Friday's Moody's review an earlier test of the country's risk assessment.

Berlin's expected cabinet decision on the ECB package comes Wednesday, the nominations deadline. The proposed chief-economist appointment and presidential backing would establish the next stage of a leadership transition as the Commission projects persistent inflation and a worsening French debt ratio. Formal political agreement remains the pending event.

Technology restrictions and Middle East security will also enter the summit diplomacy in Shenzhen. Beijing's retaliation warning raises the stakes of the remote-access dispute for companies financing overseas computing capacity. The tanker evacuation and Qeshm strikes add current operational and military developments to the energy discussion. Whether negotiations change access to chips or the security of regional shipping remains open, with both issues capable of altering financing assumptions beyond the immediate haven demand in Treasuries.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered from an initial selloff after stronger retail spending as technology disruptions shifted investors toward government debt. A reported NSA communications-network outage accompanied a sharp equity decline and a surge in Treasury futures activity. The 10-year yield fell 2.43 basis points to 5.1068%, and the 2-year declined 2.53 basis points to 4.8041%, with limited curve steepening. The 10-year real yield fell 3.62 basis points as breakeven inflation rose 1.19 basis points.

The underlying demand and inflation picture remained firm: retail control-group sales rose 0.6%, above the 0.4% forecast, and import prices increased 1.1%, including a record monthly rise in capital-goods prices. Housing showed the strain of high borrowing costs, with builder sentiment at its lowest since April 2012. Alberto Musalem advocated several rate increases before spring; John Williams rejected dramatic action and tied further tightening partly to persistent AI-driven growth. Futures fully priced a quarter-point December increase.

Credit access remained selective. Pimco argued that slower construction could support hyperscaler-backed data-center bonds by reducing supply, while HSBC's discounted sale of an Oracle-linked project loan exposed individual development risk. CCC Intelligent Solutions secured improved buyout-financing indications as JPMorgan forecast leveraged-loan defaults rising to 4.5% in 2027. Anthropic's impending IPO pricing and possible distribution of SpaceX's chip-backed debt will test financing confidence across the AI industry.
